description: Meaning that POINTS BEYOND the utterance to other meaning — essential to comprehending any speech or narrative, not a media nicety. A huge part of understanding is resolving what a thing points AT: an allusion, a quotation, a callback, a sarcastic echo all carry meaning only once the referent is recovered. This is the same operation as the babble/cross-cortex breakthrough: a grounded mapping between two representational systems IS reference. TV Tropes is dense with it (parody, homage, shout-outs, adaptations) because intertextuality is how works mean THROUGH other works — and how speakers mean through shared prior text.

concepts.name: allusion
concepts.definition: A meaning that points at another text/work/event without naming it outright, comprehensible only to a listener who can recover the referent. The pointing IS the meaning; failure to resolve it loses the sense. Generalises deixis/anaphora at the cultural scale — understanding requires holding the pointed-at as available.

concepts.name: parody
concepts.definition: Reference PLUS mocking transformation: a work invokes another's conventions and violates them to ridicule. To get a parody you must (a) recognise the target and its expectations and (b) register the violation as aimed AT it — reference fused with trope_play's subversion and humour's benign violation.

concepts.name: homage
concepts.definition: Reference PLUS reverence: invoke another work's convention to honour it. Same recognition requirement as parody, opposite affect — the violation, if any, is affectionate rather than mocking.

concepts.name: pastiche
concepts.definition: Sustained imitation of a work or style's conventions without the mockery of parody — meaning made by wearing another's frame wholesale. Comprehended by recognising the borrowed frame as borrowed.

concepts.name: adaptation
concepts.definition: A work DERIVED from another across media (book to film), carrying the source's conventions transformed by the new medium. Establishes a cross-work identity edge; understanding an adaptation often depends on holding the source as a comparison frame.

concepts.name: quotation_callback
concepts.definition: Direct re-use of prior text — a quote, catchphrase, or callback to an earlier moment (within a work or across the culture). Meaning rides on the listener's memory of the original occurrence; the second use means BY pointing at the first.
